content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am working on a web interface and would like to require a password for just one page in the navigation bar. The goal is to prevent customers from accessing that specific page. Is this possible? Alternatively, is there a way to password-protect the entire navigation? Thank you all

I am not aware of a method to assign a password to a specific page or the navigation bar within the extended web server using [product_name]. At least, this does not seem to be supported directly by the capabilities of [product_name] Web Editor. I'm also unsure if this could be accomplished with HTML5.
Alright, thank you. I will try to implement it with HTML5.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is trying to set password protection for either a single page or the entire navigation in the web interface built with [product_name], but finds that such fine-grained access control is not available using the existing features. As a result, the user is considering creating a custom solution using HTML5.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to have options for password-protecting individual pages or the whole navigation within the web interface built with [product_name], allowing for more customized access control for end-users.
